chapterTitle: Babylon the Great Prostitute and the Scarlet Beast
themeTitle: “The Lamb Will Overcome Them, for He Is Lord of Lords, and King of Kings”

scripture.text: One of the seven angels who had the seven bowls came and spoke with me, saying, “Come here. I will show you the judgment of the great prostitute who sits on many waters,
scripture.understanding: Καὶ ἦλθεν εἷς ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλων τῶν ἐχόντων τὰς ἑπτὰ φιάλας, “One of the seven angels who had the seven bowls came” — φιάλη: chapters 17–18 expand the seventh bowl's judgement on Babylon (16:19). Δεῦρο, δείξω σοι τὸ κρίμα τῆς πόρνης τῆς μεγάλης, “Come here. I will show you the judgment of the great prostitute” — κρίμα, from the judge family: the verdict, the sentence passed, as distinct from κρίσις, the act of judging (14:7); πόρνη, a prostitute: in the prophets, a city or nation that sells itself for wealth and power. τῆς καθημένης ἐπὶ ὑδάτων πολλῶν, “who sits on many waters” — ancient Babylon sat on the Euphrates and its canals; the waters are explained in verse 15.

scripture.text: with whom the kings of the earth committed sexual immorality; and those who dwell in the earth were made drunken with the wine of her sexual immorality.”
scripture.understanding: μεθ᾽ ἧς ἐπόρνευσαν οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς, “with whom the kings of the earth committed sexual immorality” — πορνεύω: political and commercial alliances that compromised with her idolatry and greed; γῆ, from the world family. καὶ ἐμεθύσθησαν οἱ κατοικοῦντες τὴν γῆν ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου τῆς πορνείας αὐτῆς, “and those who dwell in the earth were made drunken with the wine of her sexual immorality” — μεθύω, to be drunk: intoxicated with her luxury, pleasure and power, unable to see clearly.

scripture.text: He carried me away in the Spirit into a wilderness. I saw a woman sitting on a scarlet-colored beast, full of blasphemous names, having seven heads and ten horns.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἀπήνεγκέν με εἰς ἔρημον ἐν πνεύματι, “He carried me away in the Spirit into a wilderness” — ἔρημος: from the wilderness, where God keeps His people (12:6), John sees the world's true nature. καὶ εἶδον γυναῖκα καθημένην ἐπὶ θηρίον κόκκινον, “I saw a woman sitting on a scarlet-colored beast” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family); θηρίον: the beast from the sea (13:1). The city rides on the empire's power. γέμοντα ὀνόματα βλασφημίας, ἔχων κεφαλὰς ἑπτὰ καὶ κέρατα δέκα, “full of blasphemous names, having seven heads and ten horns.”

scripture.text: The woman was dressed in purple and scarlet, and decked with gold and precious stones and pearls, having in her hand a golden cup full of abominations and the impurities of the sexual immorality of the earth.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἦν περιβεβλημένη πορφυροῦν καὶ κόκκινον, “The woman was dressed in purple and scarlet” — the colours of royalty and luxury. καὶ κεχρυσωμένη χρυσίῳ καὶ λίθῳ τιμίῳ καὶ μαργαρίταις, “and decked with gold and precious stones and pearls” — the very materials of the new Jerusalem (21:18–21): Babylon is the counterfeit city. ἔχουσα ποτήριον χρυσοῦν ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτῆς γέμον βδελυγμάτων, “having in her hand a golden cup full of abominations” — βδέλυγμα, something detestable, especially idolatry. καὶ τὰ ἀκάθαρτα τῆς πορνείας τῆς γῆς, “and the impurities of the sexual immorality of the earth” — γῆ, from the world family. Golden on the outside, filthy on the inside.

scripture.text: And on her forehead a name was written, “MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF THE PROSTITUTES AND OF THE ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.”
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ μέτωπον αὐτῆς ὄνομα γεγραμμένον, μυστήριον, “And on her forehead a name was written, ‘MYSTERY’” — μυστήριον: a name with hidden meaning, to be understood spiritually. Roman prostitutes are said to have worn their names on headbands. Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη, ἡ μήτηρ τῶν πορνῶν καὶ τῶν βδελυγμάτων τῆς γῆς, “BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF THE PROSTITUTES AND OF THE ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH” — βδέλυγμα; γῆ, from the world family. Babylon destroyed Jerusalem; Rome did the same in AD 70. Peter called Rome ‘Babylon’ (1 Peter 5:13). She is the source of every idolatrous seduction.

scripture.text: I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints, and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus. When I saw her, I wondered with great amazement.
scripture.understanding: καὶ εἶδον τὴν γυναῖκα μεθύουσαν ἐκ τοῦ αἵματος τῶν ἁγίων, “I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family); ἅγιος, from the holy family: God's holy ones. She makes the nations drunk with her wine; she gets drunk on the blood of believers. καὶ ἐκ τοῦ αἵματος τῶν μαρτύρων Ἰησοῦ, “and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus” — μάρτυς, from the witness family: here plainly ‘martyrs’, those who died for their testimony. Nero's persecution in Rome was within living memory. καὶ ἐθαύμασα ἰδὼν αὐτὴν θαῦμα μέγα, “When I saw her, I wondered with great amazement” — θαυμάζω: even John is dazzled by her.

scripture.text: The angel said to me, “Why do you wonder? I will tell you the mystery of the woman, and of the beast that carries her, which has the seven heads and the ten horns.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ εἶπέν μοι ὁ ἄγγελος· Διὰ τί ἐθαύμασας; “The angel said to me, ‘Why do you wonder?’” — θαυμάζω: a gentle rebuke. The world marvels at the beast (13:3); God's people must not. ἐγὼ ἐρῶ σοι τὸ μυστήριον τῆς γυναικὸς καὶ τοῦ θηρίου τοῦ βαστάζοντος αὐτήν, “I will tell you the mystery of the woman, and of the beast that carries her” — μυστήριον. The cure for being dazzled by evil is to understand it.

scripture.text: The beast that you saw was, and is not; and is about to come up out of the abyss and to go into destruction. Those who dwell on the earth and whose names have not been written in the book of life from the foundation of the world will marvel when they see that the beast was, and is not, and shall be present.
scripture.understanding: τὸ θηρίον ὃ εἶδες ἦν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν, “The beast that you saw was, and is not” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family). A parody of God, ‘who was and who is and who is to come’ (4:8), and of the Lamb who was dead and is alive. καὶ μέλλει ἀναβαίνειν ἐκ τῆς ἀβύσσου καὶ εἰς ἀπώλειαν ὑπάγει, “and is about to come up out of the abyss and to go into destruction” — ἀπώλεια, ruin: the beast's ‘coming’ leads only to destruction. καὶ θαυμασθήσονται οἱ κατοικοῦντες ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὧν οὐ γέγραπται τὸ ὄνομα ἐπὶ τὸ βιβλίον τῆς ζωῆς ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου, “Those who dwell on the earth and whose names have not been written in the book of life from the foundation of the world will marvel” — γῆ and κόσμος, both from the world family; βιβλίον, from the book family; ζωή, from the life family. βλεπόντων τὸ θηρίον ὅτι ἦν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν καὶ παρέσται, “when they see that the beast was, and is not, and shall be present” — βλέπω, from the see family.

scripture.text: Here is the mind that has wisdom. The seven heads are seven mountains on which the woman sits.
scripture.understanding: ὧδε ὁ νοῦς ὁ ἔχων σοφίαν, “Here is the mind that has wisdom” — σοφία, from the wisdom family: as in 13:18, a call for discernment. αἱ ἑπτὰ κεφαλαὶ ἑπτὰ ὄρη εἰσίν, ὅπου ἡ γυνὴ κάθηται ἐπ᾽ αὐτῶν, “The seven heads are seven mountains on which the woman sits” — Rome was famous as the city on seven hills; Roman coins showed the goddess Roma seated on seven hills. For John's readers, the identification was unmistakable.

scripture.text: They are seven kings. Five have fallen, the one is, the other has not yet come. When he comes, he must continue a little while.
scripture.understanding: καὶ βασιλεῖς ἑπτά εἰσιν· οἱ πέντε ἔπεσαν, ὁ εἷς ἔστιν, ὁ ἄλλος οὔπω ἦλθεν, “They are seven kings. Five have fallen, the one is, the other has not yet come” — ἄλλος, from the another family. Many have tried to match these with particular Roman emperors, but it depends on where one starts counting and whom one includes, and no scheme is agreed. Seven, the number of completeness, suggests the whole line of beastly rulers, with the end near. καὶ ὅταν ἔλθῃ ὀλίγον αὐτὸν δεῖ μεῖναι, “When he comes, he must continue a little while” — μένω; δεῖ: even his brief time is appointed by God.

scripture.text: The beast that was, and is not, is himself also an eighth, and is of the seven; and he goes to destruction.
scripture.understanding: καὶ τὸ θηρίον ὃ ἦν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν, καὶ αὐτὸς ὄγδοός ἐστιν, “The beast that was, and is not, is himself also an eighth” — ὄγδοος: eight was the number of resurrection (the eighth day, the day after the Sabbath); the beast's ‘resurrection’ parodies Christ's. Many in John's day expected Nero to return. καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἑπτά ἐστιν, καὶ εἰς ἀπώλειαν ὑπάγει, “and is of the seven; and he goes to destruction” — ἀπώλεια: whatever he claims, his end is ruin.

scripture.text: The ten horns that you saw are ten kings who have received no kingdom as yet, but they receive authority as kings, with the beast, for one hour.
scripture.understanding: καὶ τὰ δέκα κέρατα ἃ εἶδες δέκα βασιλεῖς εἰσιν, “The ten horns that you saw are ten kings” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family). οἵτινες βασιλείαν οὔπω ἔλαβον, ἀλλὰ ἐξουσίαν ὡς βασιλεῖς μίαν ὥραν λαμβάνουσιν μετὰ τοῦ θηρίου, “who have received no kingdom as yet, but they receive authority as kings, with the beast, for one hour” — ἐξουσία, from the power family: delegated authority; ὥρα, from the time family: ‘one hour’, a very short time. Client rulers who share the beast's power — briefly.

scripture.text: These have one mind, and they give their power and authority to the beast.
scripture.understanding: οὗτοι μίαν γνώμην ἔχουσιν, “These have one mind” — γνώμη, purpose, decision: united against God. καὶ τὴν δύναμιν καὶ ἐξουσίαν αὐτῶν τῷ θηρίῳ διδόασιν, “and they give their power and authority to the beast” — δύναμις and ἐξουσία, two members of the power family: their ability and their authority, both handed over. People and nations surrender themselves to the beast.

scripture.text: These will war against the Lamb, and the Lamb will overcome them, for he is Lord of lords, and King of kings, and those who are with him are called chosen and faithful.”
scripture.understanding: οὗτοι μετὰ τοῦ ἀρνίου πολεμήσουσιν, “These will war against the Lamb” — ἀρνίον, from the lamb family. καὶ τὸ ἀρνίον νικήσει αὐτούς, “and the Lamb will overcome them” — νικάω: the battle of Har-Magedon (16:16) is summed up in four words. ὅτι κύριος κυρίων ἐστὶν καὶ βασιλεὺς βασιλέων, “for he is Lord of lords, and King of kings” — Daniel and Deuteronomy's titles for God, given to the Lamb. καὶ οἱ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ κλητοὶ καὶ ἐκλεκτοὶ καὶ πιστοί, “and those who are with him are called chosen and faithful” — κλητός, called; ἐκλεκτός, chosen; πιστός, faithful: God's call and choice, and their faithful response.

scripture.text: He said to me, “The waters which you saw, where the prostitute sits, are peoples, multitudes, nations, and languages.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ λέγει μοι· Τὰ ὕδατα ἃ εἶδες, οὗ ἡ πόρνη κάθηται, “He said to me, ‘The waters which you saw, where the prostitute sits’” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family). λαοὶ καὶ ὄχλοι εἰσὶν καὶ ἔθνη καὶ γλῶσσαι, “are peoples, multitudes, nations, and languages” — Babylon sits enthroned over the whole world. The same fourfold formula describes the Lamb's people (5:9; 7:9): every nation is either seduced by Babylon or redeemed by the Lamb.

scripture.text: The ten horns which you saw, and the beast, these will hate the prostitute, will make her desolate, will strip her naked, will eat her flesh, and will burn her utterly with fire.
scripture.understanding: καὶ τὰ δέκα κέρατα ἃ εἶδες καὶ τὸ θηρίον, οὗτοι μισήσουσιν τὴν πόρνην, “The ten horns which you saw, and the beast, these will hate the prostitute” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family); μισέω. Evil turns on itself: the powers that carried Babylon destroy her. καὶ ἠρημωμένην ποιήσουσιν αὐτὴν καὶ γυμνήν, καὶ τὰς σάρκας αὐτῆς φάγονται, καὶ αὐτὴν κατακαύσουσιν ἐν πυρί, “will make her desolate, will strip her naked, will eat her flesh, and will burn her utterly with fire” — the fate of Jezebel, whose flesh the dogs ate, and of the unfaithful city in Ezekiel 16 and 23.

scripture.text: For God has put in their hearts to do what he has in mind, to be of one mind, and to give their kingdom to the beast, until the words of God should be accomplished.
scripture.understanding: ὁ γὰρ θεὸς ἔδωκεν εἰς τὰς καρδίας αὐτῶν ποιῆσαι τὴν γνώμην αὐτοῦ, “For God has put in their hearts to do what he has in mind” — God's sovereignty works even through evil: the beast's purpose (γνώμη, v. 13) unknowingly carries out God's purpose (γνώμη). καὶ δοῦναι τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτῶν τῷ θηρίῳ, ἄχρι τελεσθήσονται οἱ λόγοι τοῦ θεοῦ, “and to give their kingdom to the beast, until the words of God should be accomplished” — τελέω, from the perfect family: brought to completion. The best manuscripts read λόγοι, from the word family; others ῥήματα, also from the word family. God's words will be fulfilled to the letter.

scripture.text: The woman whom you saw is the great city, which reigns over the kings of the earth.”
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἣν εἶδες ἔστιν ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη, “The woman whom you saw is the great city” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family). The plainest identification in the chapter. ἡ ἔχουσα βασιλείαν ἐπὶ τῶν βασιλέων τῆς γῆς, “which reigns over the kings of the earth” — γῆ, from the world family. In AD 95 only one city did that: Rome. But Babylon is also every city and civilisation that builds its glory on idolatry, greed, immorality and the blood of God's people.

visualMeditations.title: The Woman on the Scarlet Beast
visualMeditations.image: Picture a wilderness, and in it a scarlet monster with seven heads, covered in blasphemous names. On its back sits a woman in purple and scarlet, dripping with gold, jewels and pearls, holding up a golden cup — and on her forehead the name: ‘MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT.’ Look closer at the cup: it is full of filth.
visualMeditations.meaning: “The woman was dressed in purple and scarlet, and decked with gold and precious stones and pearls, having in her hand a golden cup full of abominations” (v. 4). The world's glamour hides corruption. What looks golden from a distance is poison up close.

visualMeditations.title: Drunk on the Blood of the Saints
visualMeditations.image: Picture the beautiful woman lifting her cup again — and it is red. She is drunk on the blood of believers. John stares, dazzled. Then the angel touches his shoulder: ‘Why do you wonder?’
visualMeditations.meaning: “I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints, and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus. When I saw her, I wondered with great amazement” (v. 6). The angel said, “Why do you wonder?” (v. 7). Do not be dazzled by a world that kills God's people. See it for what it is.

visualMeditations.title: The Lamb Wins
visualMeditations.image: Picture ten kings with their armies massed behind the beast, all marching against one small Lamb. And then the battle is over before it begins: the Lamb stands, and they fall. Around Him stand His people — called, chosen, faithful.
visualMeditations.meaning: “These will war against the Lamb, and the Lamb will overcome them, for he is Lord of lords, and King of kings, and those who are with him are called chosen and faithful” (v. 14). The outcome is never in doubt.

visualMeditations.title: Evil Devours Itself
visualMeditations.image: Picture the beast that once carried the woman turning on her, tearing off her jewels and robes, devouring her and setting her on fire — while above it all, God's hand guides even this toward the fulfilment of His word.
visualMeditations.meaning: “The ten horns which you saw, and the beast, these will hate the prostitute, will make her desolate” (v. 16). “For God has put in their hearts to do what he has in mind” (v. 17). Evil has no loyalty; it destroys its own. And God's purposes are accomplished even through His enemies.

structure.label: The Prostitute and the Beast (v. 1-6)
structure.body: One of the bowl angels shows John the judgement of the great prostitute who sits on many waters, with whom the kings of the earth committed immorality; in the wilderness John sees a woman on a scarlet beast, dressed in purple and scarlet and covered in gold and jewels, holding a golden cup of abominations, with the name ‘Babylon the great, mother of prostitutes’ on her forehead; she is drunk with the blood of the saints and martyrs, and John is amazed.

structure.label: The Mystery Explained (v. 7-14)
structure.body: The angel explains: the beast was, is not, and will come up from the abyss to destruction, and the earth-dwellers will marvel; the seven heads are seven mountains and seven kings; the beast is an eighth king belonging to the seven; the ten horns are ten kings who will reign with the beast for one hour and give it their power; they will make war on the Lamb, and the Lamb will conquer them, for He is Lord of lords and King of kings.

structure.label: The Prostitute Destroyed (v. 15-18)
structure.body: The waters are peoples, crowds, nations and languages; the beast and the ten horns will turn on the prostitute and destroy her, for God has put it in their hearts to carry out His purpose until His words are fulfilled; the woman is the great city that rules over the kings of the earth.

sections.heading: A Tale of Two Women
paragraphs: Revelation contrasts two women. In chapter 12 a woman clothed with the sun gives birth to the Messiah and is protected in the wilderness. In chapter 17 a woman clothed in purple and scarlet rides a beast and is drunk on the blood of the saints. At the end of the book a third woman appears: the bride of the Lamb, clothed in fine linen (19:7–8), who is also a city, the new Jerusalem (21:2, 9–10). Babylon is the prostitute; Jerusalem is the bride. Every human heart and every culture is drawn to one or the other.

The angel promises to show John “the judgment of the great prostitute who sits on many waters, with whom the kings of the earth committed sexual immorality” (vv. 1–2). In the Old Testament, cities like Tyre, Nineveh and even Jerusalem are called prostitutes when they sell themselves for wealth and power and chase after other gods. Babylon's ‘immorality’ is her seductive offer of luxury, trade, pleasure and security in exchange for compromising with idolatry and injustice. Kings and merchants are drunk on it (v. 2).

Her appearance is dazzling: “The woman was dressed in purple and scarlet, and decked with gold and precious stones and pearls” (v. 4). These are the very materials of the new Jerusalem (21:18–21). Babylon is a counterfeit of God's city: all its beauty, none of its holiness. And her golden cup is “full of abominations and the impurities of the sexual immorality of the earth” (v. 4).

sections.heading: Who Is Babylon?
paragraphs: On her forehead is a name: “MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF THE PROSTITUTES AND OF THE ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH” (v. 5). Ancient Babylon was the empire that destroyed Jerusalem and the temple and carried God's people into exile. For Jews and Christians of John's day, Rome had become a new Babylon: it too destroyed Jerusalem and the temple, in AD 70. Peter, writing from Rome, sent greetings from “She who is in Babylon” (1 Peter 5:13).

The angel's explanation confirms it. “The seven heads are seven mountains on which the woman sits” (v. 9) — Rome was famous as the city on seven hills. And “The woman whom you saw is the great city, which reigns over the kings of the earth” (v. 18). In John's day only Rome fitted. She was “drunken with the blood of the saints, and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus” (v. 6), as Nero's persecution had shown.

But Babylon is more than Rome. She is ‘MYSTERY’: a spiritual reality that takes shape in every civilisation that builds its glory on idolatry, greed, luxury and the oppression of God's people. Some Christians expect a final, literal city at the end; all can see her spirit at work in every age. James wrote, “You adulterers and adulteresses, don’t you know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God?” (James 4:4).

sections.heading: The Beast Who Was, and Is Not
paragraphs: The beast that carries the woman is the beast from the sea (13:1): the political power behind the city. The angel says, “The beast that you saw was, and is not; and is about to come up out of the abyss and to go into destruction” (v. 8). This is a parody of God, ‘who was and who is and who is to come’, and of the Lamb who died and lives. Many of John's contemporaries believed Nero would return from the dead or from the east; the beast's career mimics a resurrection. The world marvels at it (v. 8).

The seven heads are also “seven kings. Five have fallen, the one is, the other has not yet come” (v. 10), and the beast himself is “an eighth, and is of the seven” (v. 11). Many attempts have been made to identify these kings with particular Roman emperors, but it depends on whom one counts, and there is no agreement. The number seven suggests the complete series of beastly powers, with the end near. The eighth, who is ‘of the seven’, is the final embodiment of the beast — and ‘he goes to destruction’.

The ten horns are ten kings who rule with the beast “for one hour” (v. 12) and give him their power and authority (v. 13). Their unity is against God. “These will war against the Lamb, and the Lamb will overcome them, for he is Lord of lords, and King of kings, and those who are with him are called chosen and faithful” (v. 14). The final battle is summed up in one sentence. The Lamb wins, and His people share His victory.

sections.heading: Evil Turns on Itself
paragraphs: The most surprising part of the vision is how Babylon falls: “The ten horns which you saw, and the beast, these will hate the prostitute, will make her desolate, will strip her naked, will eat her flesh, and will burn her utterly with fire” (v. 16). The powers that carried her destroy her. Evil has no loyalty. Systems built on greed and violence eventually devour one another.

And over it all stands God: “For God has put in their hearts to do what he has in mind, to be of one mind, and to give their kingdom to the beast, until the words of God should be accomplished” (v. 17). God does not cause evil, but He rules over it, using even the plans of His enemies to fulfil His word, as He used Assyria and Babylon in the Old Testament, and as He used Pilate and Herod at the cross.

For John's first readers, this was deeply encouraging. Rome looked eternal. But God showed them its end: stripped, devoured, burned. The angel's question to John is for us too: “Why do you wonder?” (v. 7). Do not be dazzled by the world's glamour or power. Babylon is already judged, and the Lamb is Lord of lords.

ntConnection.heading: Do Not Love the World
paragraphs: John wrote in his first letter, “Don’t love the world or the things that are in the world. If anyone loves the world, the Father’s love isn’t in him. For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, isn’t the Father’s, but is the world’s. The world is passing away with its lusts, but he who does God’s will remains forever” (1 John 2:15–17). Babylon is that world, dressed up as a queen.

Paul describes God as “the blessed and only Ruler, the King of kings, and Lord of lords” (1 Timothy 6:15); Revelation gives the title to the Lamb (17:14), and in 19:16 it is written on His robe: “KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS” (Revelation 19:16).
Those with the Lamb are “called chosen and faithful” (v. 14). Jesus said, “For many are called, but few chosen” (Matthew 22:14) — the called who are truly His show it by faithfulness.

lexicon.strongs: G4204 (committed sexual immorality πορνεύω, porneúō, G4203)
lexicon.insight: Strong's: “a strumpet; figuratively, an idolater.” πόρνη is a prostitute; Strong's notes its figurative use for an idolater. The prophets called Nineveh, Tyre and even unfaithful Jerusalem prostitutes: they sold themselves for wealth, security and pleasure, and abandoned the true God. Babylon the prostitute stands opposite the bride of the Lamb (19:7). Every culture, and every heart, is courted by one or the other.

Strong's: “a detestation, i.e. (specially) idolatry.” βδέλυγμα is something that God finds detestable — especially idolatry. Daniel and Jesus spoke of ‘the abomination of desolation’ standing in the holy place. Babylon's golden cup is full of abominations, and she is ‘the mother of the abominations of the earth’. Nothing abominable will enter the new Jerusalem (21:27).

Strong's: “ruin or loss (physical, spiritual or eternal).” ἀπώλεια is utter ruin, the opposite of salvation. Jesus spoke of the broad road ‘that leads to destruction’; Judas is ‘the son of destruction’. Twice the angel says the beast ‘goes to destruction’ (vv. 8, 11): whatever its apparent resurrection and power, its destiny is fixed. Its name, Apollyon (9:11), comes from the same root.

Strong's: “a decision (the function or the effect, for or against ("crime")).” κρίμα, from the judge family, is the verdict, the sentence handed down — as distinct from κρίσις, the act or process of judging (14:7; 16:7). The angel shows John ‘the judgment (κρίμα) of the great prostitute’: her sentence has been passed. In 18:20 God has ‘judged your judgment on her’; in 20:4 judgement (κρίμα) is given to the saints.

Strong's: “select; by implication, favorite.” ἐκλεκτός, from ἐκλέγομαι (to pick out), describes those God has chosen. The Lamb's companions are ‘called (κλητοί) and chosen (ἐκλεκτοί) and faithful (πιστοί)’ — a whole theology in three words: God calls, God chooses, and those He has chosen respond with faithfulness. The beast's followers are those whose names are not in the book of life (v. 8); the Lamb's are chosen from the foundation of the world.

holySpiritRevelation.intro: In this chapter the Holy Spirit strips the glamour from the world, so you can see it clearly.

items.title: Don't Be Dazzled
items.body: Even John “wondered with great amazement” at Babylon (v. 6), and the angel asked, “Why do you wonder?” (v. 7). The Spirit wants to break the spell that the world's wealth, beauty and power cast over you. Look at the cup in her hand: it is full of filth.

items.title: Which Woman Will You Love?
items.body: There is a prostitute and a bride; Babylon and the new Jerusalem. The Spirit asks: whose embrace are you in? Where have you been seduced by the world's offers of comfort, success and pleasure? Return to your first love, the Lamb.

items.title: The Lamb Wins
items.body: “The Lamb will overcome them, for he is Lord of lords, and King of kings” (v. 14). The Spirit wants you to face the powers of the world with confidence. You are called, chosen and faithful, and you are on the winning side.

audit.title: The Glamour Check
audit.body: What in the world most dazzles you — wealth, celebrity, luxury, influence (v. 4)? Has it drawn your heart away from God?

audit.title: The Intoxication Check
audit.body: Are you ‘drunk’ on anything the world offers — so absorbed that you cannot see clearly (v. 2)?

audit.title: The Loyalty Check
audit.body: Could you be described as ‘called, chosen and faithful’ (v. 14)? Which of the three is weakest in your life?

practices.title: Unmask Babylon
practices.body: Choose one advertisement, show or online feed you see this week. Ask: what is it offering, and what does it cost the soul? Write down what you notice. Pray 1 John 2:15–17 over your heart.

practices.title: Give Away Some Gold
practices.body: Babylon is decked with gold and pearls. This week, give away something valuable — money, a possession, time — to someone in need, as a declaration that your treasure is not in Babylon.

prayerReflection: “Lord Jesus, Lamb of God, You are Lord of lords and King of kings. Open my eyes to see the world as You see it. Strip the glamour from Babylon, so that I am not dazzled by her purple and gold, nor drunk on the wine she offers. Forgive me where I have loved the world and the things in the world. Thank You for Your saints and martyrs, whose blood Babylon has shed; strengthen those who suffer today. Thank You that Babylon is already judged, that the beast goes to destruction, and that even Your enemies' plans serve Your purposes until Your words are fulfilled. Keep me with You — called, chosen and faithful. Let me belong to the bride, not the prostitute; to the new Jerusalem, not to Babylon. Amen.”

storyConnections.title: The Tower of Babel
storyConnections.summary: After the flood, people gathered on a plain in Shinar and said, ‘Come, let’s build ourselves a city, and a tower whose top reaches to the sky, and let’s make a name for ourselves.’ God came down, confused their language and scattered them. The city was called Babel — Babylon. From the beginning, Babylon is humanity's attempt to make a name for itself without God, to reach heaven by its own achievement. Revelation's Babylon is the last and greatest form of that same proud city.

storyConnections.title: Jezebel's End
storyConnections.summary: When Jehu came to Jezreel to bring God's judgement on Ahab's house, Queen Jezebel painted her eyes, arranged her hair and looked down from a window to taunt him. At Jehu's word, her own servants threw her down. When they went to bury her, they found only her skull, her feet and her hands; the dogs had eaten her flesh, as Elijah had prophesied. The queen who had seduced Israel into idolatry was destroyed by her own household. Babylon's end in verse 16 echoes Jezebel's.

storyConnections.title: Daniel and the Fall of Babylon
storyConnections.summary: King Belshazzar of Babylon threw a great feast and drank wine from the gold and silver cups taken from the temple in Jerusalem, praising gods of gold and silver. Suddenly a hand appeared and wrote on the wall. Daniel read it: God had numbered his kingdom and brought it to an end; he had been weighed and found wanting. That very night Belshazzar was killed and Babylon fell to the Medes and Persians. Revelation's Babylon, drinking from her golden cup, will fall just as suddenly.
